title: Deque Tricks (Sliding Window Max)
tagline: A double-ended queue keeps a window's maximum available in O(1) amortised.

intuition.analogy: A bouncer keeping a VIP list ordered by status: when a higher-status guest arrives, everyone behind who's lower-status is dropped — they can never be 'the most important' while the new guest stands ahead of them. The front of the list is always the current VIP.
paragraphs: The sliding-window-maximum problem asks for the max of every length-k window. A heap gives O(n log k); a monotonic deque gives O(n) by maintaining a queue of indices whose values are strictly decreasing.

Two operations keep it tidy. Before adding a new index, pop smaller values from the back (they're dominated by the newcomer and will never be the max while it's present). And pop from the front if it has slid out of the window.
The front of the deque is always the index of the current window's maximum. Each index enters and leaves the deque once, so the whole sweep is linear.
intuition.keyIdea: Keep window indices in a deque with decreasing values; the front is always the maximum, updated in O(1) amortised.

steps.title: Evict the stale front
steps.detail: If the front index is ≤ i − k, it's outside the window — pop it from the front.

steps.title: Maintain monotonicity at the back
steps.detail: While the back's value ≤ a[i], pop it; those values can't be a maximum while a[i] is in the window.

steps.title: Push and read
steps.detail: Push i at the back. Once the first window is formed (i ≥ k−1), the front index gives the current window's maximum.

complexity.spaceReason: The deque holds at most k indices.

pitfalls: Storing values instead of indices makes window-eviction impossible.
Use ≤ when popping the back to handle duplicates correctly.
Only start emitting answers once the first full window exists (i ≥ k−1).

dryRun.clickMoment: When 5 arrives, every smaller value is purged from the back at once — the deque collapses to just [5]. The dominated candidates vanish the moment they become irrelevant.

approach: Maintain a deque of indices whose values are strictly decreasing. The front is always the current window's maximum.

problems.title: Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K
problems.statement: Shortest subarray with sum ≥ K (negatives allowed).

approach: Work on prefix sums P. A subarray [l+1, r] has sum P[r] - P[l] >= K. For each r we want the largest l (< r) with P[l] <= P[r] - K.

Keep a deque of candidate indices with increasing prefix sums. Pop the front while it satisfies the condition (recording length), and pop the back while it is not smaller than the current prefix (it can never be a better left end).

problems.title: Constrained Subsequence Sum
problems.statement: Max subsequence sum where chosen indices are within k of each other.
problems.hint: DP with a sliding-window-max deque over the dp array.
problems.tests: Deque to optimise a DP transition.

approach: Let dp[i] be the best subsequence sum ending at i. Then dp[i] = a[i] + max(0, best dp in the window [i-k, i-1]).
A monotonic deque maintains the maximum dp over the sliding window of size k, giving O(n).

codes.source:
from collections import deque
class Solution:
    def constrainedSubsetSum(self, a: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(a)
        dp = [0] * n
        dq = deque()
        best = float('-inf')
        for i in range(n):
            if dq and dq[0] < i - k:
                dq.popleft()
            take = max(0, dp[dq[0]]) if dq else 0
            dp[i] = a[i] + take
            best = max(best, dp[i])
            while dq and dp[dq[-1]] <= dp[i]:
                dq.pop()
            dq.append(i)
        return best

problems.title: Jump Game VI
problems.statement: Maximise score jumping up to k steps at a time.
problems.hint: dp[i] = a[i] + max(dp[i-k..i-1]); maintain that max with a deque.

approach: dp[i] = a[i] + max(dp[i-k .. i-1]) — the best score to reach index i jumping at most k.
Slide a monotonic-decreasing deque of dp values over the window so each transition is O(1).

problems.title: Sliding Window Median
problems.hint: Two heaps (or multiset); contrast with the deque approach for max.

approach: Maintain the window as an ordered multiset so the median is read from the middle position(s).
Each slide inserts the entering value and removes the leaving one in O(log k). In C++ a multiset with a mid iterator works; in Python a SortedList gives O(log k) indexing.
